title: MHHS2402 W2 · Respiratory Anatomy II
subject: Cardiovascular, Renal & Respiratory Systems
content: Neck posterior triangle: CN XI, brachial plexus, subclavian vessels. Carotid sheath: vagus (X), internal jugular vein, common carotid. Larynx cartilages: thyroid, cricoid (only complete ring), arytenoid, corniculate, epiglottis; true cord=vocal fold. Posterior cricoarytenoid = only abductor; recurrent laryngeal supplies all intrinsic except cricothyroid. Ribs: true 1-7, false 8-10, floating 11-12. Diaphragm hiatuses: caval T8, oesophageal T10, aortic T12; phrenic C3-5 -> referred shoulder pain. Intercostal bundle VAN in costal groove; chest drain above the lower rib. Parietal pleura=somatic (pain), visceral=autonomic. Right lung 3 lobes (oblique+horizontal), left 2 lobes+cardiac notch. Type I pneumocyte=gas exchange, Type II=surfactant.

questions.question: Which laryngeal cartilage is the only COMPLETE ring?
questions.explanation: The cricoid is the only complete cartilage ring; the thyroid is a shield open at the back.

questions.question: The 'true' vocal cords are also known as the:
questions.explanation: The true cords are the vocal folds (phonation); the false cords are the vestibular folds.

questions.question: Which nerve supplies the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: The phrenic nerve (C3–C5) gives motor and sensory supply to the diaphragm.

questions.question: How many lobes does the LEFT lung have?
questions.explanation: The left lung has 2 lobes plus a cardiac notch; the right has 3.

questions.question: How many lobes does the RIGHT lung have?
questions.explanation: The right lung has 3 lobes (oblique + horizontal fissures); the left has 2.

questions.question: Which alveolar cell produces surfactant?
questions.explanation: Type II pneumocytes make surfactant; Type I pneumocytes are the thin gas-exchange cells.

questions.question: Gas exchange across the alveolar wall occurs mainly through which cell?
questions.explanation: Thin Type I pneumocytes form most of the alveolar surface for gas exchange.

questions.question: The main muscle of quiet inspiration is the:
questions.explanation: The diaphragm increases the vertical dimension of the thorax during quiet inspiration.

questions.question: Which pleura directly covers the lung surface?
questions.explanation: Visceral pleura covers the lung; parietal pleura lines the thoracic wall.

questions.question: Which muscle divides the neck into anterior and posterior triangles?
questions.explanation: Sternocleidomastoid divides the neck; trapezius forms the posterior boundary of the posterior triangle.

questions.question: Which intrinsic laryngeal muscle is the ONLY abductor of the vocal cords?
questions.explanation: The posterior cricoarytenoid is the sole abductor (opens the cords); the others adduct or tense them.

questions.question: Most intrinsic laryngeal muscles are supplied by which nerve?
questions.explanation: The recurrent laryngeal nerve (from the vagus) supplies all intrinsic muscles except cricothyroid.

questions.question: The suprahyoid muscles act to:
options: A. elevate the hyoid and larynx
B. depress the hyoid and larynx
questions.explanation: Suprahyoids (digastric, mylohyoid) elevate the hyoid and larynx; infrahyoids depress them.

questions.question: Which pleura is pain-sensitive, and why?
questions.explanation: Parietal pleura has somatic innervation (intercostal and phrenic) and is pain-sensitive; visceral pleura is not.

questions.question: True ribs (1–7) attach to the sternum by:
options: B. the costal cartilage of rib 7
questions.explanation: True ribs (1–7) each have their own costal cartilage to the sternum; false ribs share or float.

questions.question: The central non-muscular part of the diaphragm is the:
questions.explanation: Muscle fibres converge on the central tendon; the crura anchor the diaphragm to the lumbar spine.

questions.question: The oesophageal hiatus of the diaphragm is at which vertebral level?
questions.explanation: The oesophageal hiatus is at T10 (with the vagus); caval hiatus T8, aortic hiatus T12.

questions.question: In the costal groove, the intercostal neurovascular bundle runs in what order (top to bottom)?
questions.explanation: From superior to inferior in the costal groove it is Vein, Artery, Nerve (VAN).

questions.question: The cardiac notch is a feature of which lung?
questions.explanation: The cardiac notch and lingula are on the left lung, making room for the heart.

questions.question: Phonation (voice production) occurs at which laryngeal division?
questions.explanation: The glottis — the vocal folds and rima glottidis — is the phonation region of the larynx.

questions.question: The caval opening (IVC) passes through the diaphragm at which level?
questions.explanation: The caval hiatus is at T8, through the central tendon, with the right phrenic nerve.

questions.question: The aortic hiatus of the diaphragm lies at which vertebral level?
questions.explanation: The aortic hiatus is at T12, behind the diaphragm, transmitting the aorta, thoracic duct and azygos vein.

questions.question: The internal laryngeal nerve provides which function?
options: A. sensation above the vocal cords
B. sensation below the vocal cords
C. motor to the cricothyroid muscle
D. motor to all intrinsic muscles
questions.explanation: The internal laryngeal nerve (from the superior laryngeal) is sensory above the vocal cords.

questions.question: The external laryngeal nerve supplies which single muscle?
questions.explanation: The external laryngeal nerve is motor to cricothyroid, which tenses the vocal cords.

questions.question: How do the bronchial arteries differ from the pulmonary circulation?
options: A. they nourish lung tissue from the aorta
B. they carry the blood for gas exchange
C. they drain the lungs into the heart
D. they supply only the pleura
questions.explanation: Bronchial arteries (from the thoracic aorta) nourish the lung tissue; the pulmonary arteries carry blood for gas exchange.

questions.question: Why is the RIGHT main bronchus the more common site of foreign-body aspiration?
options: A. wider, shorter and more vertical
B. narrower, longer and more horizontal
C. the same shape as the left
D. blocked by the aortic arch
questions.explanation: The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical, so inhaled objects tend to lodge there.

questions.question: The conducting zone differs from the respiratory zone in that it:
options: A. has no alveoli and no gas exchange
B. holds most of the body's alveoli
C. is the main site of gas exchange
D. contains no airways at all
questions.explanation: The conducting zone (trachea to terminal bronchioles) moves air but has no alveoli, so no gas exchange.

questions.question: The right oblique fissure of the lung roughly follows which rib?
questions.explanation: The oblique fissure runs from about T4 along the 6th rib to the 6th costal cartilage.

questions.question: Phrenic nerve palsy typically causes:
options: C. complete loss of all breathing
D. spasm of the vocal cords
questions.explanation: Losing phrenic supply paralyses a hemidiaphragm, which then sits raised and moves paradoxically.

questions.question: In the pulmonary plexus, sympathetic activity to the airway causes:
questions.explanation: Sympathetic activity dilates the bronchi (bronchodilation); parasympathetic activity constricts them.
